anima.config.option.limits.reads_per_tic: How many blocks one Person may read each tick. The main performance dial.
anima.config.option.limits.queue_cap.des: How many spotted-but-unexamined columns may back up before new sightings are dropped.
anima.config.option.limits.region_max_bl: Block budget for scanning one structure; hitting it leaves the region marked as only partly known.
anima.config.option.limits.region_cache_: How much of the world's shape one world remembers on everyone's behalf, so that fifty settlers in one wood don't each scan the same trees. They still notice and remember their own trees — they just stop re-measuring them. Counted in blocks; 0 turns it off.
anima.config.option.limits.place_index_c: How many blocks' worth of recognised things — trees, ponds, patches — one world remembers for everybody, so walking up to a wood someone has already been through costs nothing to understand. Held once per thing rather than once per look, so it goes much further than the remembered shapes above. 0 turns it off.
anima.config.option.limits.reads_per_tic: Total blocks every agent on the server may read between them each tick. The per-agent budget above caps one mind; this caps the whole server, which is the only cap a growing population can outgrow. At the ceiling they notice things a little later rather than not at all, and they still see what is right beside them first. 0 turns it off.
anima.config.option.limits.rays_per_tick: Total line-of-sight checks every agent on the server may spend between them each tick. At the ceiling they notice things a little later rather than not at all — refused checks are deferred, never dropped.
anima.config.option.limits.ray_budget.de: Base line-of-sight checks per Person per tick. The real budget grows with the backlog, so a large wave of mobs is noticed within a few ticks — checks are deferred, never skipped.
anima.config.option.limits.pathfinder_in: Work out routes during the tick instead of on a background thread. Off, routes cost the tick nothing but take however long they take in real seconds — fine at normal speed, but fast-forward the world and a route that used to arrive instantly takes many ticks, so they stand about looking lost. On, a route is always ready the same tick it was asked for, at the cost of a small hitch when a crowd re-plans together. Mainly for testing.
anima.config.option.claims.ttl_ticks.des: How long a claimed work site outlives its last heartbeat before another Person may take the spot. 20 ticks is one second.
anima.config.option.journal.max_entries_: How many journal entries each Person keeps. Older ones are dropped once it fills.
anima.config.option.journal.max_age_tick: How old a journal entry may get before it is dropped. The default is 10 minutes of game time.
anima.config.option.journal.sweep_interv: How often the journal clears out entries that have aged past their lifetime.
anima.config.option.journal.file_sink.de: Also mirror each agent's journal to logs/anima/<run>/agent-<id>.log on disk.
anima.config.option.journal.keep_runs.de: How many past runs of journal files to keep. Older ones are deleted when the server starts; an agent who died keeps theirs in graveyard/.
anima.config.option.journal.death_tail_e: How many of an agent's final journal lines are kept in its grave, where they survive both the sweep and the restart. This is what the grave readout shows you when you ask why somebody died. 0 keeps only the bare tombstone.
anima.config.option.web_debugger.enabled: Start the web debugger automatically whenever a world loads. This is the auto-start switch only — /anima web-debugger start runs it for one session whatever this says. A development tool: it shows every agent's mind and its buttons command them.
anima.config.option.web_debugger.port.de: The port the web debugger listens on. Change it if something else already holds this one; run /anima web-debugger for the address either way.
anima.config.option.web_debugger.host.de: The address the web debugger listens on. 127.0.0.1 keeps it on this machine, which is what its security is built around: it shows every agent's mind and its buttons command them, and the allowed browsers below are the only thing guarding it. A LAN address, or 0.0.0.0 for every interface, puts all of that on the network over plain HTTP where a name can be read in transit. The server warns you when it binds anywhere else.
anima.config.option.web_debugger.allowed: The browsers allowed to see this world. Each browser makes up its own three-word name, keeps it, and asks to be let in; you allow it in-game with /anima web-debugger allow, which writes it here. Nothing is allowed on its own and the list starts empty. Delete a line — or run /anima web-debugger remove — to take a browser off the list; it can ask again. A name on this list works like a password: whatever presents one sees every agent here and can command them.
anima.config.option.web_debugger.app_url: Where the web debugger's interface is loaded from. The mod itself serves only a small loader page, so the site this points at never sees any of your world. Point it at a local address to work on the interface itself.

anima.config.aspect.mind.stickiness.desc: Bonus added to whatever the Person is already doing, so small swings in pressure don't leave them dithering between two urges.
anima.config.aspect.mind.preempt.desc: How much raw pressure a new urge needs before it may cut into a task already under way.
anima.config.aspect.instincts.flee_range: Distance in blocks at which a threat starts to register at all.
Distance in blocks over which fear ramps from nothing to full panic.
anima.config.aspect.instincts.flee_appro: Extra fear when a threat is measurably closing in — the observable stand-in for "it is hunting me".
anima.config.aspect.instincts.wander_idl: The do-something floor: every real drive must beat this. At 0 an unbothered Person simply stands still.
anima.config.aspect.instincts.wander_rad: How far, in blocks, an idle saunter may pick its next stop.
anima.config.aspect.senses.radius.desc: How far away, in blocks, another being can be perceived at all.
anima.config.aspect.senses.sneak_range_m: Shrinks the range at which a sneaking being is noticed. Sneaking shortens how far away you are spotted; it never makes you invisible.
anima.config.aspect.senses.invisible_ran: Shrinks the range at which an invisible being is noticed — the sneak multiplier above, turned right down. An invisible body should have to be almost within reach before it is seen at all; it can still be heard the whole time. 0 means invisibility is total to this body's eyes.
Horizontal field of view in degrees. Beings outside it go unseen until they make noise; 360 sees in every direction.
anima.config.aspect.senses.vertical_degr: Half-angle in degrees above and below where the Person is looking — human sight is wide but flat. 90 removes the up/down limit.
anima.config.aspect.senses.hearing_radiu: How far away, in blocks, noise-makers are noticed regardless of the view cone. Sneaking beings are silent; 0 makes a Person deaf.
Object permanence: how long a being stays perceived — frozen as last remembered — after both sight and sound have gone quiet.
anima.config.aspect.senses.heard_activit: How long an activity known only by sound — heard mining, a heard scuffle — stays believed after the noise stops. Afterwards only the bare presence is left.
anima.config.aspect.senses.near_interval: How often, in ticks, a being standing right there is re-checked.
anima.config.aspect.senses.far_interval_: How often, in ticks, a being at the edge of range is re-checked. Distances in between fall between the two.
anima.config.aspect.senses.attack_decay_: How long being attacked keeps something read as hostile, with or without a face on it. Much longer than the other senses on purpose: forgetting an attack fifteen seconds later is amnesia, not object permanence.
anima.config.aspect.senses.herd_link_rad: How far apart two animals of the same species may stand and still count as one herd. Herds link in chains, so a spread-out pasture still joins up.
anima.config.aspect.places.radius.desc: Horizontal sensing radius in blocks, within the cone below. Cost grows with its square — a walking Person sweeps about 2R columns per block moved.
Field of view in degrees for noticing places beyond the halo below. Narrowing it is what pays for the radius above, and is why a Person no longer notices a tree squarely behind them. 360 notices in every direction at every distance.
anima.config.aspect.places.near_radius.d: Radius in blocks within which places are noticed whichever way a Person faces — what you are standing next to, rather than what you are looking at.
anima.config.aspect.places.horizon_radiu: How far a Person makes out the gist of what is out there — a forest, not a tree. Sight rays are marched out to it, and it sets both how long they are and how many make up a fan, so raising it costs more than proportionally; the work is paid for out of whatever the near field left unspent, so what a longer reach really buys is how often the whole view is fresh. Set at or below the sense radius to switch it off.
anima.config.aspect.places.see_through_r: How far a Person's eye resolves a see-through thing — a canopy, a water surface — into its parts. Nearer than this they look between the branches; further off the same canopy is a wall the skyline stops at, which is why a Person standing in a wood can barely see out of it. 0 means they never see into anything.
anima.config.aspect.places.region_max_sp: How far a scan may spread from where it began — what splits one fused mega-forest into separate groves.
How many places of each kind a Person remembers before the stalest is forgotten. Must exceed the trees they work among, or edge trees are forgotten and rediscovered forever.
anima.config.aspect.danger.melee_mult.de: Danger multiplier for a visibly held melee weapon — a zombie with a sword outranks bare claws.
anima.config.aspect.danger.ranged_mult.d: Danger multiplier for a visibly held ranged weapon: bow, crossbow or trident.
Danger multiplier for visible armor on the body.
Danger multiplier for a mounted body, such as a skeleton riding a spider or a horse.
anima.config.aspect.danger.baby_mult.des: Danger multiplier for a baby variant — smaller, faster and harder to hit.
anima.config.aspect.social.hail_radius.d: How far away, in blocks, a shouted hail is heard. A hail has to carry further than sight or it would add nothing to simply noticing someone. This also sizes a Person's ear; quieter sounds are still limited to the hearing range.
anima.config.aspect.social.hail_patience: How long a shout is still worth answering after it's heard, and how long before this body would call the same one again. 600 ticks is thirty seconds.
anima.config.aspect.social.hail_answer_p: How much being called pulls at this body. Strong enough that someone idle comes when called; below the interrupt threshold on purpose, so a shout waits for a task's natural stopping point instead of cutting into it.
anima.config.aspect.social.company_solit: How long being completely alone takes to run this body's company all the way down. 24000 ticks is one in-game day.
anima.config.aspect.social.company_proxi: How long merely being near ONE person they have already met would take to fill their company right up. Set this longer than the time to get lonely and a single neighbour is not enough to keep them content.
anima.config.aspect.social.company_utter: How many lines of conversation it takes to fill their company right up. Counted per line said or heard, not per second spent talking — otherwise somebody slow to answer would be better company than somebody quick. The time itself still counts, as time near a person, which is what it is.
anima.config.aspect.social.company_meeti: How many new faces it takes to fill their company right up. Counted once per person, the moment a name is first learned — meeting somebody is worth something on its own, and simply standing beside a stranger is not.
anima.config.aspect.body.height.desc: How many blocks of headroom this body needs to walk through a space. A settler is 2; something one block tall squeezes under what a settler must walk around.
anima.config.aspect.body.jump_height.des: How many blocks this body can jump straight up. 0 means every step up is a wall to find a way around.
anima.config.aspect.body.max_drop.desc: How far this body will willingly drop. Anything deeper reads as a hole to route around, and the same number decides what counts as a ledge to tread carefully near.
anima.config.aspect.body.max_leap.desc: The widest gap this body can jump across. 1 is a walking jump; 2 and 3 need a sprint run-up. 3 is vanilla's sprint-jump limit.
anima.config.aspect.body.can_swim.desc: Whether this body will enter and cross water. Off keeps water impassable, so it routes around instead. Surface crossing only.
anima.config.aspect.body.can_dig.desc: Whether this body has an arm to cut its way out of somewhere with. Off does not stop it noticing that it is shut in — it means the only thing it can do about it is say so.
anima.config.aspect.escape.pressure.desc: How hard being unable to leave presses on this body. High by default: somewhere it cannot get out of makes every other urge it has about somewhere it cannot reach. Below fear on purpose — the thing chewing on you outranks the wall.
anima.config.aspect.gaze.turn_degrees.de: How far this body's head turns in a single tick — its reflexes, in the only unit you can see them in. A bird's head arrives instantly; a cow's swings round. Turn it up far enough and every glance becomes a snap.
anima.config.aspect.gaze.max_twist_degre: How far the head turns from the shoulders before the shoulders come along too. It is also what this body simply will not look at while walking, since its legs decide which way it is squared up — anything further round is let go rather than stared at over one shoulder.
The least time this body rests its eyes on one thing when nothing needs its attention. With the longest look below, this pair is its idle attention span.
The most time this body rests its eyes on one thing before looking elsewhere. Keep it above the shortest look; the other way round is read as the wider of the two rather than refused.

anima.command.config.no_such_key: No such config key "%s" — try tab-completion, or /%s config show
anima.command.not_identified: That Person isn't identified yet (still spawning).
anima.command.no_match: No agent matches '%s' — try a name or id from the list command.
anima.command.ambiguous_name: %s agents named '%s' — pick one by id: %s
anima.command.recipes.none: Nobody knows a way to craft %s.
anima.command.survey.nothing: %s has nothing to survey — places.horizon_radius is inside the sense radius, so there is no range the near field does not own.
anima.command.survey.done: %s looked all the way round from %s, %s, %s: %s made out in %s reads.
anima.command.survey.gave_up: %s looked all the way round from %s, %s, %s: %s made out in %s reads — gave up at %s%% of the turn, which is a bug or a very strange world.
anima.command.horizon.none: %s has no skyline — places.horizon_radius is inside the sense radius.
anima.command.horizon.header: %s — skyline to %s blocks across a %s° cone: %s of %s bearings walked, %s glimpsed
anima.command.profile.no_such_aspect_hin: No such aspect "%s" — try tab-completion, or "profile all"
anima.command.profile.no_modifiers: %s has no modifier set — this body's mod has not given it one, so it is exactly its species and cannot be shifted
anima.command.profile.nothing_modifying: nothing is modifying %s — "profile all" shows every aspect
anima.command.follow.whom: Follow whom? Bare `follow` means "follow me", which only a player can say — name a target: /anima follow <player>.
anima.command.follow.elsewhere: %s is in another dimension — there is nothing to walk toward.
anima.command.follow.bad_leash: far (%s) must be at least near (%s) — the order reads "get within near, once they are far away", so a shorter leash never lets them settle.
anima.command.follow.started: %s is following %s — settling %sm away, setting off again past %sm.
anima.command.brain.auto_disabled: (auto disabled — re-enable with /anima brain auto true)
anima.command.brain.auto_on: %s's brain auto is true — the arbiter is deciding.
anima.command.brain.auto_off: %s's brain auto is false — manual; hand it back with /anima brain auto true.
anima.command.brain.wander_on: %s's brain wander is true — they drift when nothing else is pressing.
anima.command.brain.wander_off: %s's brain wander is false — muted; they stand still when idle. /anima brain wander true to restore.
anima.command.needs.no_company: %s has no company gauge — that body's species does not feel lonely.
anima.command.claims.none: No site is claimed right now.
anima.command.knowledge.glimpse: %s (%s, %s, %s) - %s blocks away, made out from %s off, %s ago
anima.command.inv.wrong_slot: %s can't be worn by a Person (%s).

anima.command.select.dead: %s is dead — nothing left to command.
anima.command.select.not_loaded: Selected %s isn't loaded — /anima select clear, or select someone else.

anima.command.select.ambiguous: %s agents match '%s' — pick one by id: %s

anima.command.select.none: No selection — commands use the nearest Person.

anima.command.contacts.never_knew: You never knew who that is.
anima.command.contacts.knew_nobody: You knew nobody to begin with.
anima.command.contacts.cleared: Every name forgotten — everyone is a stranger.
anima.command.party.own: You are already in your own party.
anima.command.party.already_alone: You are already on your own.
anima.command.party.left: You left the party — on your own again.
anima.command.places.unknown_kind: No place kind is registered as '%s'.
anima.command.places.not_yours: %s is not a claim you can see.
anima.command.list.none_ever: Nobody has ever had a mind here.
anima.command.list.none: Nobody living has a mind yet.
anima.command.grave.no_words: no last words — nothing was in their journal
anima.webdebug.not_running: The web debugger isn't running — /anima web-debugger start turns it on.
anima.webdebug.app_url: the page loads its interface from %s
anima.webdebug.session_only: this session only — turn on web_debugger.enabled to start it with every world
anima.webdebug.none_allowed: no browser can see this world yet — open the page, then allow it here
anima.webdebug.exposed: bound to %s — reachable from off this machine, and there is no TLS. An allowed browser name is the only guard, and it crosses the network in the clear.
anima.webdebug.malformed_name: "%s" isn't a browser name — they look like stairs-furnace-cooked.
anima.webdebug.allowed: %s can now watch every agent in this world, and command them.
anima.webdebug.removed: %s can no longer see this world, and its stream is closed. It can ask again.
anima.webdebug.asking: A browser wants to see this world:
anima.webdebug.hover.allow: Let this browser watch every agent here, and command them
anima.webdebug.hover.allow_this: Let it watch every agent here, and command them
anima.webdebug.hover.dismiss: Drop it from the waiting list. It can ask again
anima.webdebug.hover.remove: Take this browser off the list. It can ask again
